answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 68% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the karst calculation reruns each epoch, the cipher weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the plume settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 132 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 37 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
